extracted.intended_audience: Office of Medical Services management and planning staff (CIA); Chief, Plans Staff, DDS
extracted.subtask_description: Internal memorandum reporting projected goals and implementation steps for the Office of Medical Services to comply with OMB Circular A-44 for the period 1 January–30 June 1971, focusing on management effectiveness, program planning participation, cost reduction, and laboratory automation. Includes specific timeline, planned drafting of the FY1973–1977 program plan, and metrics for laboratory throughput and reagent costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting period for projected goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Projected goals of the Office of Medical Services for the period 1 January-30 June 1971 are submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All goals and activities described are to be targeted to and measured within the six-month reporting window 1 January–30 June 1971. Use this period as the timeframe for evaluating progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Effectiveness Goals — Improved operating efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Improved operating efficiency: During this six months period we expect an improvement in operating efficiency through the continued development of a practice already started. This is the practice of bringing OMS division and staff chiefs more effectively into the program planning process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize integrating division and staff chiefs (many are MDs/PhDs whose strengths are professional) into PPB-type program planning. The metric of success is observable improvement in planning and operating efficiency resulting from this change in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program planning participation by division and staff chiefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Division and staff chiefs will work closely with our planning officials and will contribute to a greater degree than they ever have before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure by the level and substance of contributions from division/staff chiefs to the OMS Program Plan (FY1973–1977). Successful participation should produce a program submission to which these officials have made significant contributions and which yields experience that improves future planning and operating efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft OMS Program Plan for FY 1973-1977 (timeline)
rubrics_metrics.description: During January and part of February 1971 we shall be drafting the OMS Program Plan for the period FY 1973-1977.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion of the draft within January–part of February 1971 is an explicit milestone. The draft should incorporate input from division and staff chiefs as described above and serve as the program submission referenced in Management Effectiveness Goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Reduction Goals — Reduction in unit cost for laboratory testing materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduction in unit cost for laboratory testing materials: The period 1 January-30 June 1971 will be the first full six months period for the automated multiphasic biochemical profiling in the Clinical Division laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate cost reduction by comparing reagent/material costs under the new automated system versus previous manual procedures. The memo presents a concrete example and target: reagents for the SMA 12 Jr. cost $2 per battery of 12 tests versus $1 per manual test (i.e., $12 for 12 tests), implying reagent cost roughly one sixth of previous costs. Use such unit-cost comparisons to demonstrate program savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory automation throughput and reagent-cost metrics (SMA 12 Jr.)
rubrics_metrics.description: The heart of this new system is the SMA 12 Jr., a laboratory device that will automatically run 12 tests on one blood sample (30 such samples can be processed in one hour). The chemicals required by the SMA 12 Jr. — reagents — cost $2 for each battery of 12 tests whereas reagents required for tests performed manually as before cost $1 for each test — or $12 if all 12 tests were to be run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the device-specific metrics (12 tests per sample; 30 samples/hour throughput; reagent cost $2 per 12-test battery) as operational performance targets. Compare throughput and per-battery reagent cost to prior manual benchmarks to quantify efficiency and cost-effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiphasic screening to increase employee accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Our program plans provide for such a screening program to enable us to be accessible to many of the Agency employees that we do not now see.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess program success by increased coverage/accessibility to Agency employees (expanded screening reach). Link cost savings and automation (above metrics) as enablers for broader access—i.e., lower per-test cost and higher throughput should permit screening more employees who previously lacked access.
